faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Is Ziggy safe for my child?
faq.a1: Absolutely. Ziggy is GDPR-compliant, stores all data in the EU, uses end-to-end encryption, and never collects personal information from children. Parental consent is required for all accounts.
faq.q2: What ages is Ziggy designed for?
faq.a2: Ziggy is designed for children aged 5 to 12. The AI adapts language, difficulty, and content based on the child's age and learning pace.
faq.q3: Can I cancel my subscription anytime?
faq.a3: Yes, you can cancel anytime with no questions asked. Your data can be exported or fully deleted within 72 hours.
faq.a4: Ziggy supports 12 languages: French, English, Spanish, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Turkish, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, and Arabic.
faq.q5: How does the cognitive profiling work?
faq.a5: Ziggy measures 6 cognitive dimensions — speed, logic, formulation, creativity, persistence, and curiosity — through natural interactions. No tests or quizzes, just learning through play.

games.pageSubtitle: Four fun mini-games to train your memory, your maths and your logic — and learn all about AI!
games.sectionSubtitle: Learning sticks so much better when it feels like playing. Pick a game and go!

memory.name: Memory Match
memory.description: Flip the cards and find all six matching pairs. How few moves will you need?
memory.howTo: Tap a card to turn it over, then tap another one. If the two pictures match, they stay! Find all 6 pairs.

math.name: Speed Maths
math.description: Solve as many sums as you can in 60 seconds. The longer your streak, the trickier they get!
math.howTo: Pick the right answer out of four. Every correct answer grows your streak — and the questions level up with you.

logic.name: Pattern Quest
logic.description: Look at the row of shapes, work out the hidden rule and pick the one that comes next.
logic.howTo: Each row follows a rule: a repeat, an alternation, or something that grows. Choose the shape that fills the empty slot. 10 rounds!

quiz.name: AI Explorer
quiz.description: Eight questions to turn you into a real artificial-intelligence expert.
quiz.howTo: Pick an answer, then read the explanation to learn something new. There are no bad answers — only new things to discover!

options: A computer program that learns from lots of examples
A tiny robot that lives inside the screen
A kind of magic only grown-ups understand
A new video game console
questions.explanation: AI is a computer program that learns by looking at heaps of examples — a bit like you learn to recognise cats after seeing lots of them!

questions.q: How does an AI learn to recognise a cat?
options: Someone whispers the answer in its ear
It looks at thousands of pictures of cats
It was born already knowing
It asks the cat
questions.explanation: An AI is shown thousands and thousands of images. Little by little it spots what cats have in common: whiskers, pointy ears, a tail!

options: Never, it is always right
Only on Mondays
Yes, quite often — that is why we check
Only if you are mean to it
questions.explanation: Yes! An AI can sound very sure of itself and still be wrong. Always double-check important answers with a grown-up or a book.

questions.q: Is an AI alive, like an animal?
options: Yes, it eats and sleeps
No, it is a program — it has no feelings
Yes, it has a heart made of wires
It is alive only while the computer is on
questions.explanation: An AI is not alive. It feels neither joy nor sadness, even when it writes "I am happy". It is a very clever program, nothing more.

questions.q: Online, somebody asks for your home address. What do you do?
options: Give it, to be polite
Give it, but only the street name
Say nothing and tell a grown-up you trust
Post it so everyone can see
questions.explanation: Your address, your school and your phone number are private. Never share them online, and always tell a grown-up you trust.

questions.q: Where do an AI’s answers come from?
options: From texts and images created by people
From outer space
From the AI’s own imagination
From a secret library nobody can read
questions.explanation: AI learns from words and pictures made by people. That is also why it can repeat their mistakes — and why humans still matter so much.

questions.q: A friend says a chatbot is their best friend. What is true?
options: It is a real friend who loves them
It is a useful tool, but not a real friend
It is better than a real friend
It remembers their birthday because it cares
questions.explanation: A chatbot can be fun and helpful, but it does not feel friendship. Real friends are people (and pets!) who truly care about you.

questions.q: What is the best way to use AI for your homework?
options: Copy its answer word for word
Ask it to explain what you do not understand, then do the work yourself
Never use it, it is forbidden
Ask it to do everything while you watch TV
questions.explanation: AI makes a great tutor: ask it to explain! But your brain only grows when YOU do the work — and that is the best part.
